title: Empty technician columns stay visible to drop work into
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on the Work Orders build under test with Work Orders view permission and Work Orders create-and-edit; the Board View and Tech View display options are on.
  2. The current location has at least 3 lead technicians shown as groups/columns (a technician is eligible when they are Clockable, Active, and their role is not Office or Time Clock User).
  3. Via New Work Order, create several work orders and set a Lead Technician on each, spread across the technicians with some left Unassigned; then open the Work Orders page.
  4. An eligible technician with no matching work; in Board View.
custom_steps:
1. Switch to Board View.
  2. Find the empty technician column.
  3. Read its short empty state.
  4. Confirm a card can be dropped onto it.
  5. Look for any control to hide empty columns.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • A technician column with no work orders under the current filters, and an empty Unassigned column, show the text "No work orders" and stay visible as drop targets.
  • Empty eligible columns are kept as drop targets except while Assigned to me is enabled; there is no control to hide them.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043 (Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options). Story reference: SV-10046 — Board View. Spec: Confluence page 845185030 “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options”, PRD v33 (2026-09-28), requirement(s) S3-R9, S3-R20, S3-R21 (read 30 Sep 2026). Review decisions/answers: Confluence page 853901313 where cited. Source-verified on 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R9: “Keep empty eligible technician columns visible as drop targets, except while Assigned to me is enabled (S3-N1), subject to S1-N1.”
  • S3-R20: “A technician column with no work orders under the current filters, and an empty Unassigned column, show the text “No work orders”.”
  • S3-R21: “Do not offer a control to hide empty eligible technician columns.”
